author: Ashley King
title: UK Government's Draft Bill on 'Ticket Touting' Ban Included in King's Speech As Predicted, But the Music Industry is No Less Disappointed - NewsBreak
text:
By Ashley King ,
10 hours ago Photo Credit: The London Standard
As predicted, the King’s Speech on Wednesday only included the draft bill on a ticket tout ban, but the music industry is nonetheless disappointed. The UK government’s draft bill on a so-called ticket tout ban was included in the King’s Speech on Wednesday (May 13), illustrating a lack of urgency among parliamentary issues and disappointing the wider music industry.
Though this outcome was predicted previously, it is no less a blow to ticketing reform in the country. The bill’s status as a draft bill de-prioritizes the matter and will probably result in a much lengthier process than if it had been introduced as a primary government bill.
By design, draft bills are subject to scrutiny and consultation from industry groups, parliamentary committees, and consumers alike before formal introduction to Parliament as legislation. That means that any law to address ticket scalping in the UK could still be years away.
The bill would make it illegal to resell a ticket at more than its face value, place a cap on service fees, and make it illegal to resell more tickets than you are entitled to buy, as well as placing obligations on resale platforms while empowering the Competition and Markets Authority to impose strict fines.
According to the government, the draft bill will “seek to destroy the operating model of ticket touts, improve access for genuine fans when tickets originally go on sale, and end rip-off resale prices once and for all.” But many in the music industry are disappointed that the bill will not be a priority in Parliament and will be subject to consultation.
“The government’s failure to take long-promised action on the shady ticket touts and rogue businesses who continue to rip off customers is a betrayal of millions of music fans,” said Tom Kiehl, CEO of UK Music. “Until we get action on sky-high ticket resales, we will continue to see cash siphoned overseas from the wallets of UK fans and the UK music industry in order to swell the already huge profits of ticket resale businesses.”
“No definitive legislative action to stop ticket touts profiteering is disappointing,” said Sarah Slater, Ticketmaster’s UK Managing Director. “Ticketmaster voluntarily capped resale prices at face value back in 2018 and continues to invest in protecting fans with safer digital tickets, stronger bot detection, clearer pricing, and better information in the queue,” Slater added. “As long as touts are allowed to make huge profits reselling tickets on other platforms, the problem will continue.”
“Despite having been reassured by the Prime Minister in a letter to fans on Friday that there would be action ‘as soon as possible,’ the relegation of this important issue to a ‘draft bill’ in the footnotes of the King’s Speech is hugely disappointing,” said Annabella Coldrick, Chief Executive of the Music Managers Forum. “Choosing the longer path via a ‘draft ticket tout ban bill’ will also adversely impact music fans, who are already losing hundreds of millions of pounds each year to price-gouging ticket touts. Further delays will cost them dearly.”
“As the Prime Minister has made clear, we remain fully committed to stamping out ticket touting for good. For too long, fans have been ripped off, and we’re determined to right that wrong,” said a government spokesperson in response to the widespread criticism. “That’s why we are taking the time to get this right by bringing forward draft legislation to ensure that our measures are truly effective, enforceable, and future-proof, and fans get the protection and security they have always deserved.”
